text:
The biggest story in Detroit isn't on the ice. Dylan Larkin asked for a trade, lost the captaincy in September, and was suspended without pay in late October after the team said he refused to play. The trade talk has only grown since: the Wild reportedly made the best offer, and Montreal's name keeps coming up. Moritz Seider is now fielding questions about leading a team without a captain.

The hockey hasn't helped. Detroit is 7-10-3 with 17 points, winless in five (0-5-0) and outscored 18-9, and in that run it got just 42% of the expected goals. Our playoff race gives Todd McLellan's team a 15% chance.

Here's the strange part: over the full season the Red Wings have been even on chance quality (50.4% of expected goals) and have scored 10.8 fewer goals than those chances deserved. They have about four and a half fewer points than they earned. Some of this is bad finishing, not a bad team.

There are pieces to build around. Alex DeBrincat's line with rookie Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård has outscored opponents 8-1 at 5-on-5 with 63% of the expected goals. Justin Faulk and William Wallinder have been the better pair on process. But John Gibson is .851 over his last five starts, 4.8 goals worse than expected, and the losing streak won't end without saves. Watch the Larkin talks, because whatever comes back in that trade will shape this season more than any line change.
headline: The Larkin standoff hangs over the Red Wings
